text: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, people of Israel — against the whole family I brought up out of the land of Egypt:
You alone have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will call you to account for all your iniquities.
Do two walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Does a young lion growl from his den unless he has caught something?
Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground where no snare is set for it? Does a trap spring up from the earth when it has caught nothing at all?
If a ram's horn sounds in a city, do the people not tremble? If disaster comes to a city, has the LORD not done it?
Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing his counsel to his servants the prophets.
The lion has roared — who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken — who can but prophesy?
Proclaim it over the citadels of Ashdod and over the citadels in the land of Egypt, and say: Gather on the mountains of Samaria and see the great turmoil within her and the oppression in her midst.
They do not know how to do what is right, declares the LORD — those who store up violence and plunder in their citadels.
Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: An enemy will surround the land; he will pull down your defenses, and your citadels will be plundered.

This is what the LORD says: As a shepherd rescues from the lion's mouth two legs or a scrap of an ear, so shall the people of Israel be rescued — those who sit in Samaria on the edge of a bed, on the corner of a couch.
Hear this and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord GOD, the God of hosts:
For on the day I punish Israel for its transgressions, I will also punish the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.

versions.text: On the day I punish Israel for its transgressions, I will also punish the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
versions.explanation: The opening כִּי links this verse to the summons of v. 13 and is unrepresented. Adding "For" preserves the logical connection and reads naturally aloud.

text: I will strike down the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end, declares the LORD.

versions.text: I will strike down the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory will perish, and the great houses will come to an end, declares the LORD.
versions.explanation: רַבִּים means "many," not "great." The point is the sheer number of houses destroyed, not their grandeur; "great houses" misrepresents the Hebrew.
